# Mercedes-Benz Museum technical tour

Static GitHub Pages site: one page per exhibit showing its mechanism working (three.js), offline after one visit, for
iPhone/iPad Safari (iOS 16.4+, import maps). No bundler: native ES modules; `tools/build.mjs` only stamps the service worker.

## Map
- `index.html` route (lib/app/index.js) · `stop.html?s=<slug>[&r=teaser]` one stop as a scroll story (lib/app/shell.js;
  r=teaser pages among the teaser stops and links back to teaser.html): the car's stage pins while its steps (intro on the
  photo, one per component with its cards, background with the outline) scroll past and set what it shows ·
  `teaser.html` the three `teaser` stops' stories one after another (lib/app/teaser.js, own manifest) · `sw.js` offline
  cache (new root files also go in tools/build.mjs ENTRIES)
- `stops/tour.js` route order, room, level, and `teaser` (slugs): single source for order and prev/next ·
  `stops/<slug>/car.js` pure data (+ photo.jpg)
- `lib/model/` pure maths, Node-tested: linkage (multi-link closure), quarter-car (ride), engine (N-cylinder slider-crank,
  timing, diesel), blower, valvetrain (spring float, desmo), steering (double-pivot trapezoid, centre pivot, twin steered
  axles), differential (one axle; traction4: four-wheel drive with locks or brake traction control), gearbox (sliding
  gears), aero (drag, top speed), truss (space frame twist), crash, air-spring (levelling: air, or a motor-wound torsion
  bar), wankel, cooling, belt (two-speed flat-belt drive, hill climbing), hoist (car-transporter deck: cylinder, pulley
  block, cables), flow (2-D lattice-Boltzmann wind tunnel: D2Q9 + Smagorinsky, moving road, drag split), abs (tyre slip
  curves, braking with and without ABS), rollover (tip angle, rolling pendulum, roll-bar timing), hydraulics (gas
  accumulator, pump, cylinders), climate (cabin heat balance), portal (portal-axle clearance), roof (folding hardtop)
- `lib/scene/` stage (renderer, cameras, lights, theme tokens, loop), helpers, ghost-body, road, wind-tunnel (CFD view of
  `flow` on the centre plane: speed/pressure/swirl field, body section, smoke streaklines; `--cfd-*` tokens)
- `lib/app/` shell, teaser, story (scroll stories: shared by shell and teaser), viewer (one car's stage, subsystems,
  photo view and loop: one per story), panel
  (declarative widgets, API in its header), dom (`h`, `link`), offline, index, theme.css (look after
  mercedes-benz.com: black bar/hero, white page, condensed serif, black photo cards, pills), fonts/ (Instrument Serif, OFL;
  latin + latin-ext for ő/ű), lang.js (head script: saved EN/HU choice or browser language → `<html lang>`), i18n.js
  (`t`, `num`, `loadCar`, `localizePage`), i18n/hu.js (UI catalog keyed by the English text)
- `subsystems/<id>.js` one mechanism each (params documented in each file's header): linkage-suspension, inline-engine,
  roots-blower, desmo-valvetrain, steering, differential, gearbox, radiator, aero, space-frame, crumple-zone,
  air-suspension, wankel, belt-drive, hoist, abs, rollover, comfort-hydraulics, cabin-climate, portal-axle,
  four-wheel-drive, twin-steer, vario-roof. inline-engine also draws V engines (`leans`: one bank per lean angle,
  opposite cylinders sharing a crankpin) and twin ignition (`plugs: 2`); crumple-zone can carry an engine block that
  slides under the floor (`engine`)
- `tools/` build, vendor-three, camera (shared pinhole maths), fit-photo-camera (+ photo-fits/*.json), trace-profile
  (+ profile-traces/*.json: side-photo pixels → mm profile), photo-grid (crop + pixel grid + projected profile overlay, PNG
  via Playwright), stop-shot (stage screenshot + fps + page errors; needs `npm run serve`) · `docs/TOUR-POC.md` (model maths §6), `docs/research.md`
- `vendor/three/` is generated by `npm run vendor -- <version>`: never read or edit it.

## Conventions
- Vehicle frame: mm in configs, metres in the scene; x forward, y left, z up; origin per car in `frame.origin`. z = 0 is
  axle height for the first six cars, the ground for the rest: each car.js header says which.
- Camber − = top inboard · toe + = toe-in · travel + = bump · steer + = left.
- Colours only through CSS tokens (`stage.bind`, `stage.tokenMat`, `var(--…)` in SVG): never hard-code theme colours.
  `--band`/`--card` are the fixed-black areas (header bar, index hero, stop cards) and stay dark in both themes.
- Illustrative numbers get a comment in car.js and a line in `unverified` (the page shows it). Sources go in `sources`.
- Panel DOM is built with textContent only; widget ids must be unique within a component.
- English is the source; Hungarian is complete and tested. UI text: `t("English literal", ...args)` with `{0}` placeholders
  (never a variable or template as the key; whole phrases, as Hungarian case endings differ), static HTML: `data-i18n`.
  Logic never compares displayed text: keep English keys/ids and map them to `t(...)` for display. Readout numbers pass
  through `num` (decimal comma). Car text: `stops/<slug>/hu.js`, car.js's shape with only the text fields (list in
  tests/unit/helpers.mjs `TEXT`), null keeps the original; sources and credits stay untranslated.

## Contracts
- car.js: `{ slug, title, name, year, summary, eyebrow, lede, frame?, ride?, orbit?, sun?, body?: { ghost }, photo?,
  components: [{ id, label, subsystem, view: { pos, target }, ghost?: { fill, edge }, params, talk }], note, unverified, sources }`
- Subsystem: `export function create(ctx, params)` with ctx `{ stage, carRoot, frame, ride, panel, reducedMotion, t }`, returns
  `{ layout({ active, onPhoto }), update(dt, { onPhoto }) }`. lib/app/viewer.js owns photo view, outline, ghost body and
  the loop (the story's step at the reading line chooses what it shows; a car without a photo shows its model), and
  resets carRoot's pose each frame before calling the active component's `update`.

## Recipes
- Add a stop: entry in `stops/tour.js` + `stops/<slug>/car.js` (copy the closest sibling). Photo (every stop has one): 1200 px
  wide, CC licence with credit, camera fitted with `node tools/fit-photo-camera.mjs tools/photo-fits/<slug>.json` (wheel
  centres and tyre bottoms first; `focalPrior` when the points are nearly flat). Trace `body.ghost` from the photo so Car
  outline lines up. Subsystems fade their own opaque wheels and keep the body still when `onPhoto`. Tests find it via tour.js.
  Add `stops/<slug>/hu.js` (npm test lists missing text fields) and, for a new room, its name in `lib/app/i18n/hu.js`.
- Add a mechanism: `lib/model/<x>.js` + `tests/unit/<x>.test.mjs` first, then `subsystems/<x>.js`.
- Wind tunnel for an aero stop (Blitzen-Benz is the worked example; the other aero stops still show plain wind streaks):
  find a near-square side photo (Commons) → `tools/photo-fits/<slug>-side.json` (wheel hubs, tyre tops/bottoms/fronts/rears;
  `focalPrior` as the points are coplanar) → read outline pixels off `node tools/photo-grid.mjs <photo> <out.png> x0 y0 x1 y1
  3 10` → `tools/profile-traces/<slug>.json` (each group on its plane y) → `node tools/trace-profile.mjs` → clean up into
  `body.ghost` (silhouette) and the aero component's `flow.profile` (centre-plane section: round sharp noses, which separate
  at this low Reynolds number; add a driver for open cars) → check both with `photo-grid --overlay` on the stop photo →
  `npm test` (flow tests run every `flow` config for stability). Keep the tunnel near 16k cells (iPhone budget).
- Upgrade three.js: `npm run vendor -- <version>` (a release at least two weeks old), then `npm test && npm run e2e`.

## Commands
- `npm test` unit tests (models, configs, translations) · `npm run e2e` Playwright: WebKit iPhone/iPad × 4 (Hungarian pass on
  iPhone only) and Chromium offline (builds first)
- `npm run serve` dev server on :8765 (service worker off on localhost unless `?sw=1`) · `?debug` exposes `window.__tour`
- `npm run build` → `_site/` · deploy: push to main; `.github/workflows/pages.yml` tests, then deploys.

## Real-device checklist (iPhone and iPad Safari, from the Pages URL)
Portrait and landscape · light and dark · EN/HU switch · stop pages and teaser: each stage stays pinned while its steps scroll · orbit, pinch, sliders · photo overlay lines up with Car outline on · airplane mode
after one visit: index → every stop · Add to Home Screen, launch offline · iPad Split View · Low Power Mode still animates at
true speed · Web Inspector over USB shows no errors. LAN (`http://<mac-ip>:8765`) checks layout only: service workers need HTTPS.

## Open

  is shown (Cabriolet B photo vs the 1938 Streamliner); which W 111 variant (the 2013 photo is a 1964 220 S); whether the
  Victoria stop's car is the Vis-à-Vis of the photo; whether the Popemobile has diff locks.
- The 260 D photo fit rests on one wheel and the lamps (approximate); a side view would fit better. Also approximate: the
  Marie motorboat (no wheels: hull ends and propeller, assumed hull heights) and the W 196 R (wheel points nearly in a
  line, focal length pinned near 650 px). The hoist on the 1624 transporter is one plausible layout: the museum names

  bore and stroke (the 1886 motor-carriage engine assumed), OM 57 compression ratio, Blue Wonder and W 196 R drag figures,
  Milnes-Daimler gearing.
- Rooms to confirm for the stops added from docs/research.md: L 6500, Blue Wonder and 1624 in Collection 2 (research:
  L 6500 in Legend 3); Milnes-Daimler bus in Collection 1 (a Daimler Truck release says so; research: Legend 2); 190 SL in
  Collection 4, the Gallery of Names (research: Legend 4; since 2017 it is astronaut David Scott's 1959 car, while the

  Whether the Reitwagen replica is on show or on loan; whether the 500 SLC is the 1980 Bandama winner.
- Stops added from research_pt2.md (20): rooms follow its galleries (buses Collection 1, lorries 2, helpers 3, celebrities

# Under the skin — a visitor’s review

**8/10 as a museum companion.** At the 300 SL, I could see the open doors in the photograph, cut down the frame for conventional doors, and watch it twist. That experiment gives me a reason to look back at the real car. The harder part is finding the right stop from the gallery floor and knowing which of the moving numbers deserves my attention.

I would fund two changes first. Give visitors a shortcut to the room they are standing in, and put each mechanism’s most revealing experiment beside its first control. The tour already has enough exhibits and engineering detail.

| Part of the visit | Rating | What earns or costs points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recognizing the car and finding its stop | 6/10 | All 46 stops have a photo, and the cards are grouped by room. On a 393 × 659 phone viewport, Legend 6 began about 32 screen heights down the index. Looking for “Gullwing” in the English card text found the SLS AMG and missed the 300 SL. |
| Learning from the exhibit | 9/10 | The pinned model stays visible while I change the frame or open the SLK roof. I can test a prediction and see the answer. On the Gullwing, the paragraph connecting the frame to the doors was below the visible screen after I tapped the comparison. |
| Choosing how deeply to explore | 7/10 | One mechanism is enough for a satisfying stop, and 34 of the 46 stops have just one. Even a single mechanism can present controls, units, a legend and several facts before I know what to watch. |
| Using the tour between galleries | 9/10 | English and Hungarian, named previous/next links and offline access make it practical to carry. After “Ready offline” appeared, I disconnected Chromium and opened a previously unvisited Evolution II stop. Its model animated. |

## What to change first

1. **Give the index two useful shortcuts.** Keep “See the route.” Add “Three highlights” beside it, linking to the existing three-car tour, and a return link from the highlights to the full route. At the start of the route, add “Jump to a room” using the 11 existing room headings and their levels. Native fragment links can do the work. Include familiar names such as “300 SL Gullwing” in card text so the browser’s Find command works too. A visitor arriving at Level 3 should be able to go straight to Legend 6 and still see the photo cards that help identify the car. [Route page](../index.html) · [Room order](../stops/tour.js) · [Highlights](../teaser.html)

2. **Give each car one memorable question.** Use the route card to pose it, the photograph to show where to look, and the first mechanism to let the visitor discover the answer. Group the remaining material by the follow-up question it answers. The proposed flow and three worked examples follow below.

3. **Make the first photograph useful immediately.** The shared story currently creates a hidden image and reveals it after the 3D viewer initializes. A rendering failure can therefore leave someone standing at the car with an error message and the identifying photo hidden. Show the existing photo, its credit and the takeaway as soon as the story appears. Keep them readable if 3D fails. Also change the index invitation to “Scroll to see where the mechanism sits” so it describes the gesture the tour actually uses. [Viewer](../lib/app/viewer.js) · [Story layout](../lib/app/story.js)

## How a visitor should move through one car

The current route card often tells the story twice. On the 300 SL, the summary explains the doors and introduces fuel injection, then the blue pill lists “Space frame · Engine.” Both lead to the same page. Inside, the visitor encounters the experiment, five readouts, a colour key and finally the facts that explain the doors. The most useful edit is to move the answer closer to the moment the visitor can see it. [Route cards](../lib/app/index.js) · [Frame controls](../subsystems/space-frame.js)

| Moment | What the visitor sees | What belongs here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choosing from the route | Photo, familiar car name, year and one invitation | Use the room heading for location. Make the card one link. For the 300 SL, “Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing” and “Why do its doors open upwards?” are enough to choose it. Drop the repeated list of mechanisms from the pill. |
| Standing beside the car | The photo and one thing to find on the exhibit | Give the eye a destination. “Look at the high sill beneath the open door. Imagine climbing over it.” Save the explanation for the moment the frame is visible. |
| Trying the mechanism | A short prompt, the existing control and the result it changes | Group by action. Keep a comparison with its outcome, a sequence with its active phase, or an animation with the part to watch. Keep pause or replay within reach. Use a number only when it helps the visitor see the difference. |
| Deciding whether to linger | The consequence in one sentence, followed by a clearly named disclosure | Let someone leave knowing why the feature matters. Someone who wants the evidence can open “Frame loads and stiffness” right there. Keep units, model qualifications and any essential colour key beside the result they explain. |
| Looking back at the exhibit | The existing closing photo, one observation to take back to the car, then the next-stop link | On the Gullwing, come back to the metal the passenger must step over. Keep production history, sources and detailed assumptions available in the background. |

Each moment fits within the existing scroll. On a phone, the test is whether the visitor can see the model respond and understand the result before the next swipe. A detail disclosure belongs inside its mechanism’s step so opening it keeps that mechanism on the stage. [Shared story layout](../lib/app/story.js)

### Three ways to tell the story

**SLK · One mechanism, told as a sequence.** The route card can ask “Where does a steel roof go when you open it?” On the stop photo, draw attention to the join between roof and rear window. At the model, ask “Which moves first, the boot lid or the roof?” Put “Open the roof” beside the phase indicator. As the lid rises and the two roof pieces fold together, the visitor has the answer. End with the space the owner gives up. The folded roof takes up part of the boot. Put the three angle readings and hinge colours under “How the roof folds.” Keep the reference-photo caption at the image. A visitor can enjoy this whole stop without reading an angle. [SLK story](../stops/slk/car.js) · [Roof controls](../subsystems/vario-roof.js)

**300 SL Gullwing · Two mechanisms, joined by the shape of the car.** Give the frame the first experiment and a natural stopping point. The engine earns its own short chapter through a second feature the visitor can see. [300 SL story](../stops/300sl/car.js)

| What appears in the scroll | Proposed visitor-facing content | Where the depth goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At the high sill | “What would happen if those tubes were low enough for an ordinary door?” Keep the two frame choices together, with relative stiffness directly underneath. | Under “Frame loads and stiffness,” keep wheel load, twist angle, stiffness in N·m per degree and tube force. |
| Immediately after the comparison | “With the sides cut down, this model keeps about a third of its stiffness. The tall tubes give the real car its high sill, so the doors hinge from the roof.” | Keep the simplified-model qualification with the 35% result. Put the racing-frame history with the background. |
| Moving from door to bonnet | “Now follow the bonnet towards the nose. How did a tall six-cylinder engine fit under that low line?” Show its lean in the existing model. The 45° lean to the left explains the low bonnet. | Under “Fuel injection and engine timing,” group the invitation to watch the spray with slow motion, firing order and crank/cam readings. The visitor who came for the doors can move on after the frame. |

**540 K · Three mechanisms, told as one drive.** Stage the existing chapters in driving order. **Over a bump**, watch the left front wheel rise and the tyre-load trace change. Keep the trace key beside it and tuck the wheel-angle and track-width figures under “Front suspension geometry.” **On the straight**, use “Floor it” and watch the supercharger clutch engage. The clutch state answers when the extra power arrives. Rotor speed and illustrative boost belong together under “Inside the blower.” **At speed**, hold engine power constant and compare the Cabriolet B with the 1938 Streamliner. Keep the body choice and modeled top speed together, with the wind-tunnel fields available under “Where the drag comes from.” Identify the photographed Cabriolet and the Streamliner comparison where the body choice appears. This gives each swipe a reason even for someone unfamiliar with the term *Kompressor*. [540 K story](../stops/540k/car.js) · [Blower controls](../subsystems/roots-blower.js) · [Aerodynamics controls](../subsystems/aero.js)

### Pilot the grouping before editing all 46 stops

Start with these three cars. For each component, an editor should be able to finish the sentence “When I ___, I can see ___, which matters because ___.” Move the existing control, observation and shortest accurate explanation together. Give remaining material a title a curious visitor would actually open. Translate the complete prompts into Hungarian and check their wrapping below the pinned stage. The same content should work on the car’s own page and wherever it appears in the highlights.

Use the existing panels and native disclosures. Opening a detail should preserve the selected setting, current animation state and scroll context. Reuse the live readout in its new position so a measurement updates only once. In the pilot, ask a casual visitor to explain the Gullwing doors with all details closed, then ask an enthusiast to find the twist angle without losing the selected frame. Both paths should feel complete.

## What information is missing?

**For a short visit, the missing information is where to look.** Across the tour, 59 component stories already contain 229 technical talking points. The opening question, one visible feature of the real exhibit, and the consequence for its driver or passenger have more value on the first screen than another specification. Keep generous depth for enthusiasts, especially the comparisons, sources and clearly identified model assumptions.

**For finding a car, visitors need to know how closely the photo and location match.** The SLK already has a photo, but it shows a street car in Washington, D.C. That explanation comes in the background, after the interaction. Put “Reference photo of the same generation” beside the image. For uncertain rooms, put a brief qualifier next to the room name until someone has checked the exhibit on site. Start with Collection 4 and the 220 S. A gallery check here is worth more than drawing a precise floor map from uncertain locations. [SLK photo note](../stops/slk/car.js) · [Open location questions](../AGENTS.md)

## How to decide whether the changes work

- **Try the pilot on the floor.** Ask five first-time visitors to find a car from its room sign, choose a short visit from the home page, then use the Gullwing comparison and explain the door shape in their own words. A proposed pass is four of five completing each task unaided. Watch where they look back at the car and whether anyone who wants the figures can still find them.
- **Compare on the same phone before and after.** On a physical iPhone, repeat cold opens of the route and the Gullwing under the same network conditions. Record time to usable route links, first visible photo and first working control. Compare frame times while orbiting and changing a control on the Blitzen-Benz wind tunnel. Recheck on iPad and with reduced motion, VoiceOver and Hungarian labels. Investigate any repeatable slowdown before rollout.
- **Protect offline use.** The reviewed build packaged about 9.7 MiB of uncompressed assets. The proposed shortcuts and copy can reuse the current photos and models, add zero new media requests, and keep 3D off the index’s rendering path. After “Ready offline,” repeat the room jump, highlights link and an unseen stop in airplane mode. The existing offline test is a starting point. [Build](../tools/build.mjs) · [Offline test](../tests/e2e/offline.spec.mjs)

*Review basis, 18 November 2026.* I reviewed the route and content inventory at revision `59b1e58`, walked the index, Gullwing comparison, SLK roof control, language switch and highlights in iPhone-sized WebKit, and checked offline entry in Chromium. The ratings are editorial judgments. Actual gallery locations, visitor comprehension and physical-device timing still need field checks.

# Component wind tunnels for the 190 E Evo II and W 196 R

Remove the Evo’s **Road car on the autobahn** CFD step. Move its road-car comparison into the background. Give the racing car three close-ups, beginning with the rear wing, followed by the splitter and the front wheel arch. Give the W 196 R one close-up of the front wheel in its two body styles. In both stops the museum photo locates the part, and the next scroll takes the visitor straight to the airflow.

## What the visitor sees

| Part | View and action | What to watch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Evo rear wing** | Side view of the boot lid, wing and a short stretch of wake. Start at the baseline and tap **Raise flap**. Keep a faint outline of the previous flap position. | A short arrow at a fixed point above the trailing edge tips upward. Air leaving the wing carries more upward momentum. The existing whole-car calculation gives the track consequence in the details, about **34 kg more rear load and 9 kW more drag power at 200 km/h** in this model. |
| **Evo front splitter** | Side section at road level. Keep the bumper, lip and road in frame. Tap **Lip in / Lip forward**. Show the starting edge with a small tick so the travel is immediately visible. | Follow air meeting the upper face and air passing through the gap below. Use the same pressure scale for both settings. Show a pressure difference across the lip only if the local run resolves it. If the two settings have a weak flow difference, teach how one lip divides the air with two labelled paths. |
| **Evo front wheel arch** | Look down on the tyre shoulder and the outside edge of the flared arch. Begin with **Follow the air**. Show a narrow ribbon entering beside the tyre, then trace it past the flare into the air beside the door. | The sideways turn around the shoulder is visible in plan. A fixed cross-section just behind the tyre can show where the slower air ends up. Add **Flared / Reference arch** only if a slimmer contour clears the same tyre and produces a repeatable difference. The reference would be a design experiment. |
| **W 196 R front wheel** | Match the photo by starting **Enclosed**. Tap **Exposed**. In a wheel-height plan section the streamlined fairing gives way to the front tyre. Retain a small section of the inboard body as a landmark. | Follow the slow air downstream. At one fixed station in the air behind the wheel, outline the region below the same speed threshold in both cases. The visitor can point to where the wake moves or changes width. Let the computed result set the caption. Follow the comparison with the driver’s trade-off. The streamliner suited fast tracks. Exposed front wheels helped drivers place the car in corners. |

Mercedes-Benz describes a two-position longitudinal front spoiler and a retractable upper rear flap on the homologation Evo. The current raised-flap geometry is illustrative. Use the exhibit photo and period drawings to establish the final part shapes. For the W 196 R, frame the comparison as a front-corner view of two distinct racing bodies. [Mercedes-Benz on the Evo adjustments](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/4e61dcd8-fd75-47ca-830c-056734a165c2) · [Mercedes-Benz on the W 196 R bodies](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/b210a620-ecd7-42dc-b364-af3e85ff3d6c)

## What the current tooling can show

![Two equal-scale crops of the computed wing flow. The baseline flap is flat. Raising it changes the mean air direction in the marked region from slightly downward to slightly upward.](evo-wing-flow-comparison.png)

**The wing can be prototyped now.** The figure comes from the saved 3-D velocity fields. On the 28 mm grid, the mean air direction in the box changes from about 9° down to 4° up. On the 40 mm grid it changes from about 2° down to 6° up. The box samples the same physical volume on both grids, 3.75–3.92 m behind the front axle, 1.23–1.29 m high and 0.20–0.30 m from the centre line. The arrows show the direction of the mean velocity projected into the side view. Both grids support the direction of change. Their different angles favour a simple arrow in the exhibit. The underlying Evo II mesh is by marksform (CC BY-NC 4.0). [Source mesh](https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/mercedes-benz-evolution-ii-190e-983f5e165dee4e7c801a49c33f8e76f1) · [Case generator](../tools/cfd/geometry.mjs) · [Solver outputs](../tools/cfd/run.mjs)

**The splitter and arch need new geometry at finer resolution.** I compared the saved half-car solid masks cell by cell. At 28 mm, the flap changes 90 cells, the 40 mm lip extension changes 30, and the arch trim changes zero. At 40 mm the counts are 39, 26 and zero. Every exported force change for the lip falls below the project’s reporting criterion. The current renderer marks the part on the same car outline, paints two fixed slices and moves dots along saved mean-flow paths. Zoom can reveal information in those fields, but the arch cases are geometrically identical. [Evo geometry](../tools/cfd/geometry.mjs) · [Force comparison and slice export](../tools/cfd/export.mjs) · [Current renderer](../subsystems/race-aero.js)

**The W 196 R comparison misses the wheels.** Both settings produce the same 218 × 64 solid mask. The speed readout changes because the straight-line model uses different assumed drag, area and mass. The live tunnel has a moving road and a stationary body polygon in a vertical plane. It can show air passing above and below a splitter. It has no sideways velocity for flow around a wheel. [W 196 R data](../stops/w196r/car.js) · [Tunnel selection](../subsystems/aero.js) · [2-D flow solver](../lib/model/flow.js)

## How to compute the close-ups

1. **Wing first.** Re-export the local mask and velocity patch from the saved Evo volumes to try the interaction shown above. The published files contain only two fixed speed/pressure slices and pretraced paths. The full velocity fields and source mesh are present in this checkout and excluded from Git. For a dedicated local run, keep the boot and wing gap and sample the incoming flow from the original car run. Check the local result against the existing wing trend. Keep the whole-car force figures attributed to the original calculation. [3-D exporter](../tools/cfd/export.mjs) · [Local CFD inputs](../tools/cfd/.gitignore)
2. **Splitter next.** Run the existing 2-D solver offline on two fine nose sections with the same road, bumper and ride height. A 5 mm trial grid gives eight cells across the illustrative 40 mm extension and five across its 25 mm thickness. Refine it and move the domain boundaries to check the pressure pattern. Export each settled field so the visitor sees the new state on the first tap. The local section can support a statement about pressure on the lip. Front axle load requires forces and pitching moment over the car. [2-D solver](../lib/model/flow.js) · [Current lip dimensions](../tools/cfd/geometry.mjs)
3. **Use the offline 3-D solver for both front corners.** Build the tyre, real wheelhouse cavity, adjacent flank and moving road. Keep tyre size, placement and inlet conditions fixed within each comparison. Allow air to pass on both sides of the outer shoulder. The current Evo tool fills body columns to a simplified floor and puts a stationary cylinder one cell above the road. Its rotating-wall option produced artificial pumping on the stepped tyre. Before showing wheel spin, verify a resolved rotating tyre against a moving-ground wheel benchmark. A stationary-wheel comparison can demonstrate the effect of the bodywork if labelled and checked on those terms. Verify the inlet and lateral boundary placement for the cropped domain. The existing runner assumes uniform inflow and a mirror at the vehicle centre. [Voxel geometry](../tools/cfd/geometry.mjs) · [3-D solver boundaries](../tools/cfd/lbm3d.mjs) · [Experimental wheel and wheelhouse comparison](https://www.mdpi.com/1996-1073/12/17/3340)

For each new case, inspect the solid mask before solving. Record the local quantity the visitor will see, such as the face-to-face pressure difference or the wake width at a fixed downstream station. Check its direction on two grids and its variation over multiple settled time windows. The present 3-D runs operate far below the car’s full-scale Reynolds number. A component run can support a local observation. Whole-car drag, axle load and top speed need their own evidence. [Run conditions](../tools/cfd/run.mjs) · [Current force reporting](../tools/cfd/export.mjs)

## Phone interaction and acceptance

Use the existing pinned story with a separate camera target for each part. Show one close-up at a time in portrait. Put the prompt, two named positions where applicable, and one sentence describing the result beside the stage. Switch the solid outline and its computed field together. Hold camera, inlet speed, colour range and tracer seeds fixed across settings. Keep an outline, a direction arrow or a wake contour visible when paused. Put pressure/speed choices and modelling notes in the existing detail disclosure. The same control and takeaway should fit in Hungarian. [Story steps](../lib/app/story.js) · [Viewer cameras](../lib/app/viewer.js) · [Panel controls](../lib/app/panel.js)

Serve compact paired fields and paths from the stop folders so the existing service worker caches them. Check a cold offline opening after the tour reports ready. On an iPhone, pause, switch settings and ask a visitor to point to what changed in the air before opening the details. Repeat with reduced motion and on iPad. If they can find the moving bodywork but need a number or a legend to find the airflow change, revise the view or teach the single-state effect. The wing figure demonstrates a local signal. The splitter and both wheel comparisons still need their local runs and device checks. [Offline build](../tools/build.mjs)

# Evo II and W 196 R component airflow implementation proposal

Replace the Evo’s two whole-car airflow views with three experiments, **rear wing → front splitter → front wheel arch**. Replace the W 196 R centre-line tunnel with one **enclosed / exposed front wheel** experiment. The museum photo locates each part. Scrolling brings it into close-up. One tap should reveal something the air does, even with the animation paused.

The deliverable is four component steps, their offline data, English and Hungarian copy and tests. The Evo’s road-car comparison moves into its background note. The W 196 R’s straight-line estimate can go in its technical facts, labelled as a separate calculation. Both engine steps follow the airflow experiments. [Earlier proposal and figure](component-cfd-proposal.md) · [Evo stop](../stops/190e-evo2/car.js) · [W 196 R stop](../stops/w196r/car.js)

## Evidence to carry into implementation

| Finding from the current checkout | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Compared with the Evo baseline, the 28 mm half-car mask changes **90 cells for the flap, 30 for the lip, zero for the arch**. At 40 mm the counts are **39, 26, zero**. All four published force-change flags for the lip are false. | The archived wing is a usable visual reference. The splitter needs a finer grid. The arch needs geometry that actually includes the flare and wheelhouse opening. A closer camera alone cannot recover them. |
| Above the wing’s trailing edge, the mean air direction changes from **8.6° down to 4.0° up** on the 28 mm grid and **2.3° down to 5.7° up** on the 40 mm grid. | Put a direction arrow at the same physical patch in both settings. Keep the earlier model’s roughly **34 kg extra rear load and 9 kW extra drag power at 200 km/h** in the technical detail, explicitly attributed to the whole-car run. |
| The W 196 R body buttons produce identical **218 × 64** solid masks. Both use one vertical section between the wheels. Drag, area and mass inputs change in a separate road-load calculation. | Compute the air around the front corner in 3-D. A horizontal slice through those results can show air moving around the tyre. |
| The live solver uses a 2-D lattice, one side-profile mask, a moving road and stationary solid walls. The offline 3-D runner uses uniform inflow, a mirrored half-car, a simplified floor, stationary stepped tyres and a much lower Reynolds number than the vehicle. Its browser export contains two fixed scalar slices and pretraced paths. | Reuse the 2-D solver offline for the splitter and the 3-D kernel for the wing and wheels. Each new run covers the part and the adjacent geometry that shapes its flow. Export only the region the visitor sees. Treat the wing crop from the old full-car run as a prototype and cross-check. |

[Wing comparison image](evo-wing-flow-comparison.png) · [3-D geometry](../tools/cfd/geometry.mjs) · [Run settings](../tools/cfd/run.mjs) · [Published case metadata](../stops/190e-evo2/cfd/cfd.json) · [Current export](../tools/cfd/export.mjs) · [2-D solver](../lib/model/flow.js)

## Visitor interaction

| Step and default | Visitor action | Visible response and acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Evo wing**, side view of the boot, wing and short wake. Start at baseline. | Switch **Baseline / Flap raised** for the existing illustrative geometry. | Keep the old flap position as a thin outline. A fixed box above the trailing edge contains a mean-flow arrow. The flap and arrow both change. The nearby streamlines make the upward turn readable while moving. |
| **Evo splitter**, road-level side view of bumper, lip and ground. Start retracted. | Switch **Lip in / Lip forward**. | A tick marks the original leading edge. Follow two air paths from ahead of the bumper, one passing above the lip and one below. The pressure shading uses one scale. If the setting difference is weak, use the travel mark for position and teach how each setting divides the air. |
| **Evo arch**, plan view over the outer front tyre shoulder. Start with the fitted flare. | Tap **Follow the air** to highlight a computed path. | Keep its starting point visible and trace where the air turns beside the wheel into the flank. Paused or with reduced motion, show the complete path with arrowheads. Add a slimmer reference contour as a second case only if it clears the same tyre and produces a repeatable, visible difference. |
| **W 196 R wheel**, wheel-height plan view. Start enclosed, matching the exhibit photo. | Switch **Enclosed / Exposed**. | Show the change in fairing shape and the slow-air wake together. A short line across the flow marks the same downstream station. Highlight where its speed falls below a fixed fraction of the inlet speed. The caption names the observed change in width or position. In the details, explain why the open car gave the driver a better view of the wheels in corners. |

Use one full-width view in phone portrait. Keep the camera, seed points, inlet speed, field range and guide position fixed when switching a pair. Changing component chooses a new camera. Keep **Pause airflow** available while either state is selected. Give the result a shape as well as a colour, and put the result sentence beside the control. Use the existing technical disclosure for the legend and model assumptions. Mercedes-Benz documents two front-spoiler positions and a retractable upper flap for the homologation Evo. The current model’s raised plate is an illustrative setting. [Mercedes-Benz on the Evo adjustments](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/4e61dcd8-fd75-47ca-830c-056734a165c2) · [Mercedes-Benz on the W 196 R body styles](https://media.mercedes-benz.com/en/article/b210a620-ecd7-42dc-b364-af3e85ff3d6c)

## Work order

Each row can be assigned as a separate coding task. The model suggestions indicate where numerical judgement matters. The wing exporter and renderer can be exercised together before a new solve finishes. Run the wheel case with the clearly distinct W 196 R bodies first, then reuse the working method for the subtler Evo flare.

| Task | Suggested owner | Input | Return for review |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Reproduce the baseline and export the wing crop | Sonnet, high | Existing Evo volumes | Two decoded crops, mask counts and signed wing probe angles on both grids |
| B. Implement playback and wire the Evo wing | Sonnet, high | A’s files and the contract below | Working baseline/raised/pause controls, EN/HU, two paused phone captures and a passing interaction test |
| C. Compute the local wing and splitter | Opus, medium | A’s wing reference, nose/wing geometry | Grid and time-window comparison for each part, compact fields, and the exact claim each supports |
| D. Compute W 196 R and Evo wheel flow | Opus, medium | Photo-based front-corner geometry and the 3-D kernel | Mask sections, matched-condition runs, wake comparison and the result for the optional arch toggle |
| E. Finish both stops and verify offline | Sonnet, high | B plus accepted C/D outputs | Final story order, bilingual copy, package sizes, targeted tests and mobile/offline results |

### A. Reproduce the wing reference

1. From the repo root check for `tools/cfd/evo2.glb` and `tools/cfd/out/{base,flap}-{28,40}.{json,bin,solid}`. The mesh and raw outputs are ignored by Git. This checkout has them. A clean checkout can run the published site from its committed assets. To regenerate a missing reference volume with the original mesh, use e.g. `node tools/cfd/run.mjs flap 28 9000`. Repeat only the missing case/grid pairs. Use the recorded mesh credit. If both mesh and volumes are unavailable, continue the splitter and wheel work; record the wing reference export as pending. The published scalar images cannot reconstruct an off-centre velocity field. [Ignored inputs](../tools/cfd/.gitignore) · [Mesh source and transform](../tools/cfd/mesh.mjs)
2. Add an offline entry point, proposed as `tools/cfd/part.mjs`. Give its first operation, `node tools/cfd/part.mjs wing reference`, one job: read the two base/flap pairs, sample the probe, and write the 28 mm display crop under the ignored `tools/cfd/out/wing-reference/`. Refactor the raw reader out of the existing exporter if sharing it. Importing it must have no write side effects. Keep the original whole-car commands usable. [Volume layout and reader](../tools/cfd/export.mjs)
3. In a raw 3-D file the four Float32 blocks are density, rearward velocity, lateral velocity and upward velocity. For `N = nx * ny * nz`, the cell offset is `(k * ny + j) * nx + i`. Its centre in mm is `[x0 - (i + 0.5)*h, (j + 0.5)*h, (k + 0.5)*h]`. Check for `16*N` bytes of field data and `N` mask bytes. Average the rearward and upward velocities over **x −3920…−3750, y 200…300, z 1230…1290 mm**. Compute `atan2(meanUp, meanRearward)` in degrees. Expect 48 fluid cells on the fine grid and 12 on the coarse grid, with the four angles above. Use actual rearward flow as the arrow’s horizontal direction.
4. Recreate the figure’s 28 mm crop by selecting cell centres in **x −4300…−3150 and z 810…1420 mm**, at **y = 238 mm**. This yields 41 columns × 22 rows. Its first column / bottom row centre is `[-3171, 238, 826]` mm. Colour by vertical speed divided by inlet speed, on the same −0.25…+0.25 range for both cases. Read the flap and boot outlines from the selected solid mask. Keep the full-precision volume for deriving the overlaid arrow and paths. [Reference image](evo-wing-flow-comparison.png)

### B. Build one component player and prove it with the wing

**Ownership.** Adapt `subsystems/race-aero.js` and its Evo configuration together. It already owns the precomputed case controls, theme mapping and tracer drawing, and the Evo is its only current caller. Reuse the same subsystem for each new part. Leave `subsystems/aero.js` serving the other stops. The story already supplies a step and an orbit target for each component. [Component loader and visibility](../lib/app/viewer.js) · [Story and disclosure layout](../lib/app/story.js) · [Current CFD player](../subsystems/race-aero.js)

**File contract.** Use one `field.json` and one `<case-id>.bin` per state under `stops/<slug>/cfd/<part>/`. Start with one scalar field per part. The manifest declares the plane, location, cell spacing, dimensions, scalar quantity, shared display range and case IDs. Each case carries its computed paths and guides in vehicle mm. Here is the wing reference header to use in the first round-trip test.

```json
{
  "plane": "xz",
  "originMm": [-3171, 238, 826],
  "cellMm": 28,
  "width": 41,
  "height": 22,
  "quantity": "vertical-speed-over-inlet",
  "range": [-0.25, 0.25],
  "cases": {
    "base": { "lines": [], "guides": [] },
    "flap": { "lines": [], "guides": [] }
  }
}
```

Rows run from bottom to top. Advancing a column always decreases vehicle x. Advancing a row increases z for `xz` or y for `xy`. The origin is the **centre of the first cell**. Each binary is exactly `width * height` bytes in row-major order. Reserve 255 for solid. Quantize the common scalar range into 0…254 with rounding and clamping. Draw solid cells opaquely so the moving part remains legible. A path is an ordered array of `[x,y,z]` points. Give each guide a `kind` of `arrow` or `line` and a `points` array in the same frame. The empty arrays above illustrate the header; the display assets must contain the measured guide and the paths that the lesson uses. Keep labels in translated stop data. Keep run provenance, input geometry, both-grid results and raw units with the generation tools.

1. Start with `lib/model/part-field.js` and `tests/unit/part-field.test.mjs` for the pure format/mapping logic used by the exporter and player. A tiny asymmetric 3 × 2 fixture should catch a left/right mirror, row flip, misplaced half cell, bad byte count or solid decoded as a field value. Check both plane orientations, endpoints of the colour range, and the generated manifest’s case IDs against the stop config.
2. Reuse the stage’s camera, materials, `THREE.DataTexture` and existing path helpers. Share one texture and bounded geometry per component across taps. Use the same mm→m conversion on solids, paths and guides. Drive tracer positions from the exported mean-flow paths and elapsed time. The static field, mask and guide must remain readable at zero animation speed. Rebuild colours through CSS tokens on theme changes. One-sided velocity arrows must point aft on the car where rearward lattice velocity is positive. [Scene helpers](../lib/scene/helpers.js) · [Camera and theme API](../lib/scene/stage.js)
3. Use `params.data`, `params.start` and the existing `params.cases[{id,label,say}]` convention. Load the manifest and requested cases once per instance. Keep selection and pause state independent of fetch completion. On a rapid A → B → A switch, display the last selection. Apply the solid, field, paths, guide and result sentence as one state after data is ready. Check HTTP status and byte length. On failure show a translated message and allow retry, with the museum photo and story still usable. Return the normal `layout` / `update` pair. Show this group only when `active && !onPhoto`. Repeated story entries and settings changes must reuse or dispose GPU objects.
4. Use panel radio-style buttons with stable case IDs and `aria-pressed`, one pause toggle and a `text: { id, value }` result so the panel announces state changes. Start with stationary tracers under reduced motion. Store settings through the panel’s existing replay handlers. Keep them working when a language switch restores the selection before the assets finish loading. Set both component ghost opacities to zero for the model close-up. Keep photo identification and the closing photo outline in the existing viewer. [Panel API and state replay](../lib/app/panel.js)
5. Give the wing a near-side camera framing the boot edge, flap and short wake. For a first fit, try target `[-3.73, 0.238, 1.12]` and position `[-3.73, 1.88, 1.12]` in metres, then check both orientations. The side camera on +y puts downstream toward screen right. Set the camera on entering a step and let the visitor retain an orbit or zoom while comparing settings. Keep the archived result identified as a crop of the whole-car simulation until C supplies the local wing case.

**Done when** two paused stage captures show different flap outlines and different arrow directions at the same box. Check this before adding the other components. An updated button label alone is insufficient.

### C. Compute the local wing and splitter

**Repeatable offline runs.** Add the local cases behind `part.mjs`. A useful command contract is `node tools/cfd/part.mjs <wing|splitter|w196-wheel|evo-arch> <solve|export>`. These are proposed commands to implement. Each `solve` runs the component’s specified cases/grids into its own ignored output directory. Each `export` validates the complete case set, then publishes the compact display assets to its stop folder. Keep partial runs out of that folder. Check in the small geometry inputs and the generator, so regular builds and CI can use the committed exports without rerunning CFD. Preserve any external input’s source, assumptions and regeneration instructions.

**Local wing.** Build a domain around the wing, its gap above the boot, and the boot surface that feeds the gap. Resolve the hinged or extended portion from a documented profile or label the archived geometry as illustrative. Keep the baseline and changed geometries registered. Use the original full-car baseline’s upstream mean velocity profile to supply the same approach flow to both local runs. Save that small sampled inlet and its station with the case inputs. The current D3Q19 kernel initializes a uniform inlet. If extending it, accept a plane of inlet velocities, apply the existing equilibrium-distribution rule at fluid inlet cells, and retain the uniform default. Verify uniform-plane equivalence on a small grid. Keep enough upstream/downstream clearance for the measured turn to survive moving the boundaries. Compare the new local probe across grids and against A’s reference. If the local result disagrees, investigate inlet position, wing gap and resolution; the archived crop remains a labelled reference. [3-D solver](../tools/cfd/lbm3d.mjs)

**Splitter.** Draw two closed nose sections from the same bumper profile and ride height. Extend the lip longitudinally. The current 40 mm travel and 25 mm thickness are illustrative. Start at 5 mm per cell, which gives eight cells of travel and five through the plate, then repeat at finer spacing, for example 2.5 mm. Use `rasterize()` and `createTunnel()` from the existing 2-D model in Node. Allow fluid above and below the lip and continue the underside past the visible crop. Keep the road moving and the local domain larger than the on-screen view. Fix the model Reynolds number across refinements by scaling lattice viscosity with the feature length in cells at the same lattice inlet speed. Sample `cp(c)` on fluid cells beside each face over a stated chord interval and average over settled steps. Trace the two paths from fixed inlet seeds in the mean velocity field. Put the pressure map and old-edge tick in the export. If the face-pressure *change between settings* falls inside the variation, keep the position toggle and describe the visible upper/lower paths. Omit a front-axle load estimate. [Live solver functions](../lib/model/flow.js) · [Lip geometry](../tools/cfd/geometry.mjs)

Created [Evo II and W 196 R component airflow implementation proposal](/Users/kunabel/workspace/MercedesExperience/docs/component-cfd-implementation-proposal.md).

It breaks the work into five tasks sized for Sonnet High or Opus Medium. Each task names its inputs, files, implementation steps, and acceptance checks. It includes the data format, solver settings, EN/HU integration, offline tests, and what to do when a simulated difference is too small to show visitors.

The wing comes first because its airflow change reproduced on both saved grids. It gives the implementer a verified reference for the close-up player before tackling the splitter and wheels. The central acceptance test is that **a visitor can pause the view, switch settings, and point to what changed in the air**.
